Draft:

Raymond III Count of Tripoli was a prominent noble in the Crusader states during the twelfth century. He inherited the County of Tripoli after the death of his father Raymond II in 1152. His early years were marked by efforts to consolidate power amid rival factions and external threats from Muslim neighbors. He sought alliances with the Kingdom of Jerusalem and the Knights Templar to strengthen his position. Throughout his rule Raymond III faced internal strife as local nobles challenged his authority. He also dealt with the growing influence of the Ayyubid dynasty under Saladin.

*Early Life and Inheritance*
Raymond III was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and his wife Hodierna. He received a typical noble education focused on martial training and Latin literacy. Upon his father death he became count while still a minor. His mother acted as regent until he reached majority. During this period the county experienced raids from Nur ad Zen and later from Saladin forces. Raymond III worked to secure the coastal cities and to fortify key castles such as Tripoli and Gibelet.

*Military Campaigns and Alliances*
In the 1160s Raymond III joined King Amalric I of Jerusalem in campaigns against Egypt. He contributed troops to the siege of Damietta though the effort ultimately failed. He also negotiated truces with Muslim leaders to protect trade routes. His diplomatic skills were evident in the Treaty of 1171 which recognized his rights over certain inland territories. Raymond III supported the Knights Hospitaller in defending the northern frontier. He participated in the Battle of Montgisard in 1177 where Crusader forces defeated Saladin.

*Later Reign and Death*
The later years of Raymond III rule were dominated by the looming threat of Saladin unification of Muslim lands. He attempted to maintain neutrality while preserving his county independence. In 1187 after the disastrous Crusader defeat at Hattin Raymond III found himself isolated. He surrendered Tripoli to Saladin later that year ending Crusader control of the county. Raymond III died in captivity shortly after the fall of the city. His legacy is remembered as a ruler who navigated complex political landscapes during a turbulent era of Crusader history.
